notes.title: “Today you will be with Me in Paradise”
notes.intro: Jesus’ promise to the criminal crucified with him is often discussed in relation to what happens at death.

views.label: The believer is with Christ immediately after death
views.summary: Most Christians read this as showing that those who die in Christ are with him at once, awaiting the resurrection of the body.

views.label: A promise about the future, punctuated differently
views.summary: Some read “I tell you today, you will be with Me in Paradise,” meaning a future promise, since they believe the dead sleep until the resurrection.
views.source: Seventh-day Adventist Fundamental Beliefs, 26; New World Translation punctuation

notes.common: Ancient Greek manuscripts had no punctuation, so translators decide where the comma goes.
